content_html:
The weather in Machu Picchu is one of the most important factors when planning your trip.

It doesn’t just affect your photos…
it completely defines your experience.

Many travelers make the mistake of not considering the season… and end up dealing with rain, fog, or poor visibility.

What is the weather like in Machu Picchu?

Machu Picchu has a subtropical mountain climate, which means:

  • Moderate temperatures all year round
  • High humidity
  • Unpredictable weather changes

You can experience sun, rain, and fog… all in the same day.

Dry season (April – October)

Characteristics:

  • Sunny days and clear skies
  • Better visibility
  • Lower chance of rain

Advantages:

  • Spectacular photos
  • Better overall experience
  • Ideal for trekking (Inca Trail)

Disadvantages:

  • More tourists
  • Higher prices
  • Need to book in advance

This is the best season to visit Machu Picchu.

Rainy season (November – March)

Characteristics:

  • Frequent rainfall
  • More fog and mist
  • Greener landscapes

Advantages:

  • Fewer tourists
  • Lower prices
  • More peaceful atmosphere

Disadvantages:

  • Possible low visibility
  • Slippery paths
  • Constant weather changes

In February, the Inca Trail is closed for maintenance.

Shoulder season (March – April / October – November)

Characteristics:

  • Mix of sun and rain
  • Fewer tourists than peak season

Ideal for:

  • Travelers looking for balance
  • Good weather without large crowds

A great option if you plan carefully.

⏳ What is the best time to visit?

It depends on your travel style:

  • Best photos → Dry season
  • Save money → Rainy season
  • Balance → Shoulder season

There is no single “best” time… only the best time for you.

Key recommendations

  • Book in advance during the dry season
  • Bring waterproof clothing year-round
  • Plan early time slots (better weather)
  • Be prepared for sudden weather changes

Why is the weather so important?

Because Machu Picchu is not just a destination…

It’s a visual and emotional experience.

And the weather can enhance it… or ruin it.
